title: Espresso Brownies

items.raw: ½ cup (113 g) unsalted butter, cut up
¼ cup (55 g) packed light brown sugar

steps.text: Set it to 350°F. Line a 9×9-inch pan with parchment, leaving an overhang on two sides to lift the brownies out.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, or in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring until smooth. Let cool 5 minutes.
Whisk in both sugars, then the eggs one at a time, then the espresso powder, vanilla, and salt. Whisk hard for a full minute after the last egg — this is what gives the top its shiny, crackly crust.
Sift the flour and cocoa over the bowl and fold with a spatula just until no dry streaks remain. Fold in the chocolate chips if using.
Spread in the pan and bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is set and a toothpick in the center comes out with moist crumbs, not wet batter. Err toward underbaking.
Let cool completely in the pan, at least 2 hours, then lift out and cut into 16 squares. Warm brownies fall apart.

notes.label: Espresso powder
notes.text: instant espresso dissolves into the batter; ground coffee does not and stays gritty. It makes the chocolate taste deeper rather than making the brownies taste like coffee.

notes.label: Clean cuts
notes.text: chill the cooled slab 30 minutes and use a long knife wiped clean between cuts.

notes.label: Storage
notes.text: airtight for 4 days, or wrapped individually and frozen for 3 months.

openQuestion: Whose brownies are these, and when do they get made? This is a best guess — a dense, fudgy brownie with espresso in the batter. Tell me if yours have a glaze, nuts, or chocolate chips.
